stemMd: According to Table 4, at which of the following water temperatures did Salt P and Salt Q dissolve in most nearly equal masses?
explanationMd:
"Most nearly equal" means the smallest gap between the two columns, so take the difference row by row and compare the sizes:

- $10\;^{\circ}\text{C}$: $35.7 - 21.0 = 14.7$ g
- $25\;^{\circ}\text{C}$: $38.0 - 36.0 = 2.0$ g
- $40\;^{\circ}\text{C}$: $64.0 - 36.4 = 27.6$ g
- $55\;^{\circ}\text{C}$: $96.0 - 36.9 = 59.1$ g

The smallest gap by a wide margin is $2.0$ g, at $25\;^{\circ}\text{C}$.

Check it without arithmetic. Salt P climbs steeply while Salt Q is almost flat near $36$ g, so the two columns can only be close where Salt P's value passes through the mid-thirties — and that happens at $25\;^{\circ}\text{C}$, where Salt P reads $38.0$ g. Below that row Salt P is well under Salt Q; above it, well over. A crossing like that happens once, which is why exactly one row can be the answer. Note also that the gap is worth measuring as a size, not a signed value: at $10\;^{\circ}\text{C}$ Salt P is the smaller of the two, and at every hotter temperature it is the larger.

distractorRationale.d: At $10\;^{\circ}\text{C}$ the two masses are $21.0$ g and $35.7$ g, a gap of $14.7$ g. This is the row picked by a reader who looks for the smallest numbers in the table rather than the smallest difference between the two columns.
distractorRationale.b: At $40\;^{\circ}\text{C}$ the masses are $64.0$ g and $36.4$ g, a gap of $27.6$ g. The $36.4$ g looks close to the $38.0$ g one row above it, so this row is chosen by a reader who compares Salt Q with the wrong row of Salt P instead of comparing the two columns within a single row.
distractorRationale.c: At $55\;^{\circ}\text{C}$ the masses are $96.0$ g and $36.9$ g, a gap of $59.1$ g — the largest of the four rows offered. It is chosen by a reader who assumes the columns must converge as the temperature rises, without subtracting.

accessibilityText: The question compares the Salt P and Salt Q columns of Table 4 row by row. At 10 degrees Celsius, Salt P 21.0 grams and Salt Q 35.7 grams. At 25 degrees, Salt P 38.0 and Salt Q 36.0. At 40 degrees, Salt P 64.0 and Salt Q 36.4. At 55 degrees, Salt P 96.0 and Salt Q 36.9. All masses are per 100.0 grams of water. The four choices are the temperatures 10, 25, 40 and 55 degrees Celsius.

independentSolve.workingNotes: Differences between P and Q: 10 C is 35.7 vs 21 (14.7 apart); 25 C is 38 vs 36 (2.0 apart); 40 C is 64 vs 36.4 (27.6 apart); 55 C is 96 vs 36.9 (59.1 apart). They are closest at 25 C.

review.notes: Author solved the item and then tried to defend each distractor. The four gaps are 14.7, 2.0, 27.6 and 59.1 g, so 25 C is the unique minimum and the nearest rival is more than seven times larger; the result is the same whether the gap is read as a difference or as a ratio (P/Q = 0.59, 1.06, 1.76, 2.60), so there is no absolute-versus-proportional ambiguity here.
